॥ Om, by the universally renowned instruction, Om ॥ 1/2/1 ॥

Om. In this section, the primary tendency of the syllables that are in the form of the Linga (symbol) toward Vishnu is indicated. The omnipresence of Vishnu is declared by the statement, “Brahman is all-pervading.” This is understood to be the case because, as stated in the passage beginning with “The essence of this is the Aditya (Sun),” the Aditya is perceived as such. Therefore, it was declared: “By the universally renowned instruction.” The Narayana who is spoken of everywhere, as indicated by the passage beginning with “That which is this bodiless, self of knowledge,” is the same. The word “Brahman” is used to refer to that very entity, as is evident from the statements: “That is the supreme Brahman of the sages,” “He who is the great supreme Brahman,” and “Who is there beyond Vasudeva to whom the word Brahman is applied? For he is complete with all qualities; others are so called only by convention.” Thus, by the universally renowned instruction of the word Brahman, it is established that it refers to that very entity. ॥ 1 ॥
